content.comment_body: Hello, I have [product_name] running on a Raspberry Pi to monitor my [product_name] setup. It generally works well except for the function block diagram shown in the attachment. My goal is for the garage light to stay on for a set period, then turn off automatically. On the RS block, I must invert the Reset; without this inversion the entire diagram behaves incorrectly. The other inputs are typically network-based, but I've set them as regular inputs for testing. These are necessary to display on/off status in [product_name]. Removing the invert connector causes functionality issues.

If I've got your question right, the screenshot you posted offers a working solution. One thing that isn't clear: If the light is supposed to turn off with a delay after pressing I4, why use a comfort switch? Wouldn't a simple delayed switch-off accomplish this?

If I want to keep the light on in the garage longer, I hold I4 for 2 seconds—this keeps the light on until I switch it off again. Usually, I just switch the light on when entering, and after 2 minutes it automatically turns off. That's the function I'm aiming for, and I want this to be visible in [product_name].
Try the following setup: After switching on, if you want to turn the garage light off, make sure that I4 is not pressed for more than 0.99 seconds during the light-on duration.
Thanks for your help. This resolves my issue.

analysis.insight_summary: A user faced challenges setting up a function block diagram for automated garage lighting, attempting to integrate both timed switch-off and manual override while ensuring feedback in external monitoring software. The main difficulty was implementing logic for the invert connector to achieve desired behavior and display status in [product_name]. The user sought flexible control and accurate visualization.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the lighting logic to handle both timed automatic switch-off and manual override via button, with status accurately shown in [product_name]. Stable and reliable operation from both the hardware and the monitoring software is anticipated.
